page: Amazon Web Services x8g.4xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the custom 64-bit ARM architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. The CPU configuration provides a single thread per core, backed by 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. This instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark data highlights the memory subsystem as a primary strength of this instance. The Passmark memory score ranks in the top tier (top 10%), supported by strong large-block uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 292.71 GB/sec for read operations and 124.24 GB/sec for write operations. Database operations also show strong performance, scoring 23,817.9 in Passmark database tests. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench text processing also fall into the top 25% performance tier. Conversely, the instance exhibits limitations in LLM inference workloads, with text generation on a small model performing in the bottom 10% and prompt processing on a medium model categorized as weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the x8g.4xlarge offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The combination of dedicated physical cores and top-tier memory performance makes this instance highly suitable for in-memory databases, caching layers, large-scale text processing, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
